subject: Urban Planning
title: Spot Zoning: Corruption in Map Form
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Spot Zoning: Corruption in Map Form.

hook.text: Spot zoning is when a city changes the rules for one parcel to benefit one owner. Courts call it illegal favoritism.

buildup.text: A developer wants to build a tower in a low-rise zone. The council rezones just that parcel. Neighbors are furious.

discovery.text: Spot zoning benefits the connected and powerful. Regular homeowners can't get their lot rezoned for a duplex.

twist.text: Proving spot zoning in court is hard. Cities claim every rezoning serves the 'public interest.' Judges defer.

climax.text: Comprehensive upzoning — changing entire zones, not single parcels — is the reform answer to spot zoning.

punchline.text: Change the rules for one lot: corruption. Change them for all: reform.

quiz.question: What makes spot zoning legally problematic?
options: It increases property taxes for the affected parcel
It changes rules for one parcel, creating illegal favoritism
It requires environmental review that delays construction
